speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers the shooting sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The pain when eating suggests possible nerve involvement, specifically trigeminal neuralgia affecting the ear, but we must confirm the surgical site. Did the shooting pain start immediately after the operation, and do you notice any facial muscle weakness or numbness on that side?

REQUEST IMAGES: [Post-op CT of Right Ear/Mastoid]

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Occipital Nerve Entrapment (C2) presenting as referred otalgia.

The history of pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and difficulty wearing earrings (pressure on the mastoid) following tympanoplasty is characteristic of occipital nerve entrapment, where surgical manipulation or scar tissue compresses the nerve. We can confirm this by checking for tenderness over the mastoid and the back of the head.
